title: Cape Cod Cranberry Blueberry Muffins
changes_from_base: Plumped dried cranberries join the blueberries in a Greek yoghurt batter; the mix makes 16 slightly smaller muffins and has no lemon sugar.
summary: Soft Greek yoghurt muffins with plumped dried cranberries and fresh blueberries.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Plump
steps.text: Put the dried cranberries in a heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and leave to soften. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and line 16 muffin holes.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk the 200 g flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a bowl.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In a large bowl whisk the melted butter and sugar, add the vanilla and eggs, then the yoghurt until smooth. Fold in the dry mix with a spatula.

steps.title: Berries
steps.text: Drain the cranberries well, toss them with the blueberries and the 1 tbsp flour, then fold them gently through the batter.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Fill the cases two-thirds full and bake 18-20 min, until golden and a cocktail stick comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool 5 min in the tins, then move to the rack.

tips: The most common mistake is skipping the soak; hard dried cranberries pull moisture from the crumb.
Tossing the berries in flour helps them stay suspended.
Frozen blueberries can go in straight from the freezer; add 2 min baking.
storage: Keep in an airtight box for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
